body.heading: Words for the sky
paragraphs: Every day, the sky does something — and we have words for all of it. Weather words help us decide what to wear, what to play, and when to come inside.
Look out of the window while you read. Which words fit your sky today?

body.heading: Sunny, cloudy, rainy
paragraphs: Sunny — The sun is out and the sky is mostly clear. A sunglasses day.
Cloudy — Clouds cover much of the sky, like a gray blanket.
Rainy — Water falls from the clouds in drops. A boots-and-umbrella day.

body.heading: Breezy, stormy, foggy
paragraphs: Breezy — A light wind moves the leaves and your hair.
Stormy — Strong wind, heavy rain, and maybe thunder and lightning. An inside day.
Foggy — Tiny water drops float in the air and make everything look soft and near things hard to see.

body.heading: Snowy and icy
paragraphs: Snowy — Soft white flakes fall and cover the ground.
Icy — Water has frozen hard and slippery on paths and puddles. Walk like a penguin!

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Dress a character for three kinds of weather from this chart. What changes each time?
2. Dark clouds gathering often mean rain is coming. What other weather clues can you spot in nature?

takeaway: Weather words — sunny, cloudy, rainy, breezy, stormy, foggy, snowy, icy — describe what the sky is doing and help us get ready for it.
